processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Casting ingot homogenized at 1100 °C for 2hr after melting-casting in an open-air induction furnace.
Hot forged to 50% thickness reduction in the temperature range 1050-800 °C, followed by air cooling to room temperature.

Soaking at 1100 °C for 2hr; hot rolled in the range 1050-800 °C in two passes with reheating at 1100 °C for 5 min between passes; finally water quenched to room temperature from the finish rolling temperature (~800 °C).
Surface machining up to 1 mm depth on both sides of the hot rolled sheet to remove surface oxide layer.
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: 1 mm depth per side (final sheet thickness 3 mm)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot rolled 3 mm sheet (hot rolled & quenched, HRQ) intercritically annealed at 750 °C for 180 minutes, followed by air cooling to room temperature. Denoted IA750_180 Min.

structures.overall_structure: After intercritical annealing at 750 °C for 180 min, the microstructure consists mostly of intercritical ferrite (α) together with untransformed austenite; reverted austenite is almost completely dissolved into intercritical ferrite (only few residual fine needle/globular features). The δ-ferrite retains its structure/morphology unchanged, confirming highly stable δ-ferrite. Compared to the HRQ state, prior martensite dissolution is almost completed.

unmapped_findings: IA750_180 Min austenite volume fraction: ~30% before tensile test and ~27% after tensile test (Rietveld analysis of XRD, Fig. 7c / Fig. 7a-b).
Product of strength and elongation (PSE) for IA750_180 Min = 3.1 GPa% (Table 3), the second-lowest among the annealed conditions, attributed to a lower TRIP effect.

Mechanical stability parameter K of austenite for IA750_180 Min cannot be unambiguously assigned: the text states that at 120 and 180 min the austenite shows relatively higher mechanical stability, while the green K-curve labels in Fig. 7c read 2.198 and 1.618 for the last two conditions (values 3.216/1.929/1.079/1.618/2.198 are printed but not explicitly keyed to individual conditions).
In IA750_180 Min, dissolution of prior martensite has been almost completed, so nearly equal UTS and TE values are observed for IA750_120 Min and IA750_180 Min.
Complete dissolution of reverted austenite in IA750_180 Min occurs by elemental partitioning of Mn and Al to adjacent untransformed austenite, resulting in a low/negligible TRIP effect.
Mean work-hardening rate (stage S2) of IA750_180 Min is 1500-900 MPa; the WHR curve plunges below zero at the end of S2.

δ-ferrite in IA750_180 Min shows no significant change in elemental distribution compared to the rolled and other annealed specimens (Al 5.85±0.03, Mn 6.62±0.22 wt.%), supporting formation of highly stable δ-ferrite during solidification.
Nanoindentation hardness was not reported for the IA750_180 Min specimen; Table 2 covers only Hot rolled & quenched, IA750_5 Min and IA750_60 Min.

Fracture surface of IA750_180 Min (Fig. 11h) exhibits quasi-cleavage mode of fracture; the major portion of the fracture surface shows cleavage, indicating brittle failure due to the high fraction of δ-ferrite.
